title: Add measure-content.mjs so a deleted or gutted sheet row fails the acceptance bar
description: ADDENDUM 2 Required fix 1. measure-edge, measure-jitter and measure-mirror all pass on a blank cell, which is how six deleted NPC action rows got through Verify. Add and commit tools/spritecut/measure-content.mjs as a sibling of the existing measure-*.mjs tools, in their style (positional argv, raw RGBA input files, console.log output, zero dependencies, no ImageMagick needed). Argv: <before.rgba> <beforeW> <after.rgba> <afterW>. Height of each buffer = buffer.length / (W*4); rows are fixed at 12 x 96px, named walk-s, walk-n, walk-e, walk-w, idle, till, plant, water, harvest, carry, talk, wipe-brow. For each row it counts pixels with alpha > 16 across the full sheet width in both buffers and prints one line per row: row name, before count, after count, percent kept. A row with before > 0 and after == 0 is marked `<<< DELETED`; a row with before > 0 keeping under 80% is marked `<<< UNDER 80%`; either sets process.exitCode = 1. Rows keeping more than 100%, and rows with before == 0, pass. Add measure-content.mjs to the SCRIPTS list in tests/character-sheets-recut.test.js (the 'committed' existence check). This ticket does NOT run the tool against the committed NPC sheets — those are still the broken re-cut on this branch and t-003 owns fixing them and the real-sheet integration run. Do not touch src/, data/, assets/, tools/gen-art.mjs, or anything under reports/.
acceptanceCriteria: tools/spritecut/measure-content.mjs exists, is committed, imports only node: built-ins, and is listed in the SCRIPTS existence check of tests/character-sheets-recut.test.js

Run as `node tools/spritecut/measure-content.mjs <before.rgba> <beforeW> <after.rgba> <afterW>`, it prints exactly 12 per-row lines, each naming the row (walk-s ... wipe-brow in sheet order) with its before ink count, after ink count and percent kept, where ink is a pixel with alpha > 16
A row whose before ink is 100 and after ink is 0 is marked DELETED and the process exits non-zero
A row whose before ink is 100 and after ink is 79 is marked UNDER 80% and the process exits non-zero
When every row goes 100 -> 90, or 0 -> 0, or keeps more than 100%, the process exits 0 and prints no DELETED or UNDER 80% marker
Before and after buffers of different widths (e.g. 256 vs 448) are each read with their own width argument, so a sheet re-placed into wider cells is compared row for row
seamsNote: measure-content only READS raw RGBA buffers its caller supplies; it writes no state another code path reads. The seam between the real rebuilt NPC sheets and this checker is driven end-to-end in t-003.

entrypoints.realRunProof: it writes synthetic RGBA buffers to temp files, spawns `node tools/spritecut/measure-content.mjs <before> <beforeW> <after> <afterW>` as a child process with the real argv, and asserts on the child's actual stdout and exit status; nothing imports the script in-process.

rationale: The captain ordered the acceptance hole closed FIRST: until a check fails on a deleted row, no NPC rebuild can be proven. It is a self-contained CLI with its own synthetic-buffer tests, so it lands independently and t-003 then uses it as its gate. Running it on real sheets is deliberately left to t-003, because those sheets are still broken on this branch and would make this ticket's tests un-greenable.

title: Let measure-edge and measure-jitter check a sheet's own frame table
description: measure-edge.mjs and measure-jitter.mjs hardcode the player frame table 4,4,4,4,2,3,2,3,3,2,2,3, so a fourth NPC frame in an action row, or the player's four idle cells, is never checked for clipping or head jitter. Give each tool an OPTIONAL trailing argument: a comma-separated frames list of 12 integers (e.g. `4,4,4,4,4,3,2,3,3,2,2,3`). measure-edge: `<raw> <W> <CW> [frames]`; measure-jitter: `<raw> <W> <CW> <CH> [frames]`. When the argument is given the tool iterates exactly those cells per row; when it is absent the tools behave byte-for-byte as today (existing table, the 'N of 36' wording the captain's Definition of Done quotes). Do not otherwise rewrite either tool; measure-mirror.mjs is unchanged (it only reads walk-e/walk-w columns 0-3). Do not touch src/, data/, assets/, replace-cells.mjs, build-characters.mjs, or reports/.

acceptanceCriteria.text: measure-edge.mjs run with no frames argument on the committed player raw prints a line starting `0 of 36 cells touch a cell edge`, exactly as before
acceptanceCriteria.serves: `edge.mjs` reports **0 of 36 cells touching a cell edge** for all four sheets. Today every sheet is 36 of 36.

acceptanceCriteria.text: measure-edge.mjs run with the player's manifest frames list as a trailing argument counts sum(frames) cells (38 for frames 4,4,4,4,4,3,2,3,3,2,2,3) and prints `0 of 38 cells touch a cell edge` on the committed player sheet
acceptanceCriteria.serves: `edge.mjs` reports **0 of 36 cells touching a cell edge** for all four sheets. Today every sheet is 36 of 36.

acceptanceCriteria.text: measure-edge.mjs with a frames argument reports a cell beyond the default table (e.g. column 3 of the till row) as touching an edge when that cell's ink reaches a cell edge in a synthetic raw buffer
acceptanceCriteria.serves: `edge.mjs` reports **0 of 36 cells touching a cell edge** for all four sheets. Today every sheet is 36 of 36.

acceptanceCriteria.text: measure-jitter.mjs with a frames argument includes every listed column in a row's headX list and jitter, so a synthetic sheet whose fourth till cell's head is offset by 6px reports till jitter >= 6px with the argument and the default (3-cell) value without it
acceptanceCriteria.serves: `jitter.mjs` reports head jitter **of 1.0px or less** on every walk row of every sheet. (Originally written as "under 1px", which Celestino's measured 1.0px would fail on a technicality. 1.0px is the bar.) Today: player walk-south 5.9px, player walk-west 4.1px, rosa walk-south 6.2px, celestino walk-south 5.6px, hank walk-north 4.6px.

acceptanceCriteria: measure-jitter.mjs run with no frames argument prints the same 12 lines as before for the committed player sheet
seamsNote: both tools only READ a raw RGBA buffer and an argv; they write no state any other path reads. Feeding them the manifest's frames for the rebuilt NPC sheets is t-003's seam.

entrypoints.realRunProof: its runTool helper spawns `node tools/spritecut/measure-edge.mjs <raw> <W> <CW> [frames]` as a child process on a raw file decoded from the committed PNG (or a synthetic raw written to a temp file) and asserts the child's real stdout.
its runTool helper spawns `node tools/spritecut/measure-jitter.mjs <raw> <W> <CW> <CH> [frames]` as a child process with the real argv and parses the child's real per-row stdout lines.

rationale: NPC rows gain a fourth populated cell once the hardcoded table is dropped (t-003); without a frames argument those cells would ship unchecked for clipping and jitter. It is a distinct behaviour from content counting (t-001), so it is its own ticket, and keeping the no-argument default byte-identical preserves the captain's '0 of 36' wording.

title: Rebuild the three NPC sheets from main's committed art so every authored row and frame survives
description:
ADDENDUM 2 Required fixes 2 and 3, plus the manifest. Root cause (verified on this branch): tools/spritecut/build-characters.mjs does not read the NPC sheets committed on main; it calls generateAll() from tools/gen-art.mjs, upscales gen-art's procedural 32x48 NPC sheets 200% and hands those to replace-cells.mjs. gen-art leaves till/plant/water/harvest/carry/wipe-brow transparent, so those rows came out with 0 ink and talk kept ~38%. Separately, replace-cells.mjs hardcodes FRAMES=[4,4,4,4,2,3,2,3,3,2,2,3], dropping a fourth NPC cell wherever one exists.

Work: (1) Commit main's three NPC sheets as build sources at assets/sources/npc_celestino-64x96.png, npc_hank-64x96.png, npc_rosa-64x96.png, extracted with `git show main:assets/sprites/npc_<id>.png`; each is 256x1152 and its `git hash-object` must equal `git rev-parse main:assets/sprites/npc_<id>.png` (verify with git cat-file / hash-object, never working-tree md5); record the three blob ids. Never use the broken 448-wide NPC sheets on this branch as input, and read nothing under reports/. (2) Fix build-characters.mjs in place: for each NPC, toRaw() its committed 64x96 source directly (no 200% resize) and call replace-cells.mjs with `256 64 96 112 96` as now; remove the generateAll path and import and update the header comment. The player path (recut-from-source.mjs from assets/sources/player-source.png) is unchanged and the rebuild must still reproduce the committed player.png exactly. (3) Fix replace-cells.mjs in place, do not rewrite it: replace the hardcoded FRAMES with a scan of all 4 columns of all 12 rows, keeping every cell with any alpha > 16 (the existing `if(b<0) continue` guard applied to every column); keep one shared scale min(1, ...) (never enlarge), feet on a baseline 3px above the cell bottom, head centre of mass on the cell centre line, each figure in its own source column; never reintroduce bounding-box centring. It also prints one `frames=[...]` line of per-row inked-cell counts, which build-characters.mjs passes through to its log. (4) Run `node tools/spritecut/build-characters.mjs` and commit the three rebuilt 448x1152 RGBA NPC sheets. (5) Update data/asset-manifest.json for npc_celestino, npc_hank, npc_rosa: frames = the per-row inked-cell counts of the committed rebuilt sheet (confirm the inked cells are contiguous from column 0), populatedRows = every row with ink (expected all 12); width 448, height 1152, cellW 112, cellH 96 and key order unchanged. If an NPC idle row has only 2 inked cells, frames[idle] = 2 (sheetCell then returns [idle,0] for the NPC's default south frame, the same cell as today; do not invent standing poses). Player entry keeps its frames (idle 4) and all 12 populatedRows unless a scan of the committed player sheet disagrees. The scale may come out at or below the ADDENDUM table's 0.958/1.000/0.989 because extra cells can only widen tallest/widest; record the actual scale.

Tests to update ONLY where they encode the bug: tests/sprite-sheets.test.js 'npc_rosa ... not in populatedRows draws from idle' (its precondition 'till is unpopulated on npc_rosa' encodes the defect) becomes till index 1 -> [till,1] and an index past frames[till] clamps to the last frame, keeping the talk and walk-w assertions; keep the 'unpopulated anim falls back to idle' behaviour covered by a synthetic sheet entry (the mockSheets pattern in tests/idle-facing.test.js). tests/idle-facing.test.js 'the four committed character entries carry a 4-frame idle row' pins the NPC frames to the player table; it becomes player frames unchanged and NPC frames equal to their scanned counts. tests/character-sheets-recut.test.js: the baseline test reads each sheet's own manifest frames (replacing the cellsIn NPC idle special case); the jitter assertion becomes j <= 1.0; measure-edge and measure-jitter are also run with each sheet's manifest frames (t-002's argument) beside the default '0 of 36' run; add the measure-content integration. tests/gen-art-characters.test.js and tests/gen-art.test.js stay as they are (they describe gen-art output in a temp dir and already exempt HAND_AUTHORED_SHEETS); do not edit tools/gen-art.mjs.

Render code is NOT in scope: the tile re-centring in art.js drawFromSheet, the held facing cell in sheetCell (STAND_COL) and the two-tile walk cycle in anim.js are already on this branch and stay as they are; add no new state, flags or render paths. Do not touch src/sim/, data/movement.json, the seven protected data files (crops, water-rights, market, geopolitics, livestock, npcs, equipment), any balance number, or reports/.

Proof to record in the ticket output: measure-edge (default table and manifest frames), measure-jitter (manifest frames), measure-mirror and measure-content for all four sheets, with player measure-content using main's committed 256x1152 assets/sprites/player.png as before (read via git cat-file; report percentages as-is). Screenshots from the real game driven headless: all four held walk directions, standing still in all four facings, hoe/shovel/watering swings, and at least one NPC on screen; open every screenshot and list any not opened. Visual quality of the figures is judged by the captain at Verify. At the gate, state explicitly if any NPC figure still looks footless after re-placement (that needs new art) and that the weak walk-south stride is out of scope.

acceptanceCriteria.text: assets/sources/npc_celestino-64x96.png, npc_hank-64x96.png and npc_rosa-64x96.png are committed, each a 256x1152 PNG whose git blob id equals the blob of main:assets/sprites/npc_<id>.png, and the three blob ids are recorded in the ticket output
acceptanceCriteria.serves: `assets/sprites/player.png` is re-cut from `reports/capture/new-sprites/SOURCE-player-v2.png` into a 448x1152 sheet of 112x96 cells, and the three NPC sheets are re-cut the same way from their own sources. The captain chose the 112x96 cell (candidate C) over keeping 64x96 and shrinking the character.

acceptanceCriteria: tools/spritecut/build-characters.mjs no longer imports tools/gen-art.mjs or calls generateAll, and reads each NPC from assets/sources/npc_<id>-64x96.png

tools/spritecut/replace-cells.mjs contains no hardcoded per-row frame table, keeps every source cell that has a pixel with alpha > 16 in any of the 4 columns, and prints a `frames=[...]` line that appears in build-characters.mjs output

`node tools/spritecut/measure-content.mjs` run with before = each committed assets/sources/npc_<id>-64x96.png (W 256) and after = the committed assets/sprites/npc_<id>.png (W 448) exits 0, and every one of the 12 rows has after ink > 0 (till, plant, water, harvest, carry, talk and wipe-brow included)

acceptanceCriteria.text: Rebuilding with `node tools/spritecut/build-characters.mjs <tmpdir>` reproduces all four committed character sheets pixel for pixel (player unchanged)
acceptanceCriteria.serves: `assets/sprites/player.png` is re-cut from `reports/capture/new-sprites/SOURCE-player-v2.png` into a 448x1152 sheet of 112x96 cells, and the three NPC sheets are re-cut the same way from their own sources. The captain chose the 112x96 cell (candidate C) over keeping 64x96 and shrinking the character.

acceptanceCriteria.text: measure-edge.mjs prints `0 of 36 cells touch a cell edge` on all four committed sheets with the default table, and `0 of N` (N = sum of that sheet's manifest frames) when given the sheet's manifest frames
acceptanceCriteria.serves: `edge.mjs` reports **0 of 36 cells touching a cell edge** for all four sheets. Today every sheet is 36 of 36.

acceptanceCriteria.text: measure-jitter.mjs given each sheet's manifest frames reports jitter <= 1.0px on all four walk rows of all four committed sheets (exactly 1.0 passes)
acceptanceCriteria.serves: `jitter.mjs` reports head jitter **of 1.0px or less** on every walk row of every sheet. (Originally written as "under 1px", which Celestino's measured 1.0px would fail on a technicality. 1.0px is the bar.) Today: player walk-south 5.9px, player walk-west 4.1px, rosa walk-south 6.2px, celestino walk-south 5.6px, hank walk-north 4.6px.

acceptanceCriteria.text: measure-mirror.mjs reports all four walk-west frames `drawn facing west  ok` and no WRONG verdict on all four committed sheets
acceptanceCriteria.serves: `mirrortest.mjs` reports all four walk-west frames facing west on every sheet. Today the player's frames 2 and 3 are drawn facing EAST, so the character reverses every half cycle while walking left. The NPCs are already correct.

acceptanceCriteria: On every committed character sheet, every cell listed by that sheet's manifest frames in the walk and idle rows has its lowest pixel with alpha > 16 at y = 92 (3 clear rows above the cell bottom)

acceptanceCriteria.text: In data/asset-manifest.json the npc_celestino, npc_hank and npc_rosa entries keep width 448, height 1152, cellW 112, cellH 96 and their key order; each frames[r] equals the number of inked cells (contiguous from column 0) in row r of the committed sheet, and populatedRows lists every row that has ink
acceptanceCriteria.serves: `data/asset-manifest.json`: the four character entries become `width: 448`, `cellW: 112`. `cellH` stays 96.

acceptanceCriteria: The player manifest entry's frames and populatedRows equal the inked-cell scan of the committed player sheet (idle row 4 frames, all 12 rows populated)

Through a real createSheetLoader over the committed manifest, drawSprite for npc_rosa with {facing: 'south', anim: 'till', index: 1} blits [till, 1], and an index past frames[till] blits [till, frames[till] - 1]; talk and walk-w blits are unchanged
An anim whose row is absent from populatedRows still falls back to the idle row, proven on a synthetic sheet entry
An NPC drawn with no frame still blits [idle, 0]

measure-edge, measure-jitter, measure-mirror and measure-content output for all four sheets is recorded in the ticket output, with player measure-content run against main's committed 256x1152 assets/sprites/player.png as before

acceptanceCriteria.text: npm test passes in full, including the determinism pin and its seven historical control pins, with no file under src/sim/, data/movement.json or the seven protected data files changed
acceptanceCriteria.serves: The full suite passes, the determinism pin and its seven historical control pins included.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Screenshots from the real game driven headless are captured and opened for all four held walk directions, standing still in all four facings, the hoe, shovel and watering swings, and at least one NPC on screen; any screenshot not opened is listed
acceptanceCriteria.serves: Proof is screenshots from the real game, not sheet inspection: all four walk directions held, standing still in all four facings, and the hoe/shovel/watering swings.

seams.producer: tools/spritecut/build-characters.mjs (driving replace-cells.mjs) writes assets/sprites/npc_<id>.png from assets/sources/npc_<id>-64x96.png
seams.consumer: tools/spritecut/measure-content.mjs reads the before/after RGBA and judges per-row ink retention
seams.roundTripProof: it runs the real `node tools/spritecut/build-characters.mjs <tmpdir>`, decodes the NPC PNGs that command actually wrote plus the committed 64x96 sources to raw RGBA files, and spawns the real measure-content.mjs on those bytes, asserting exit 0 and after > 0 on every row; no ink count or payload is typed into the test.

seams.producer: replace-cells.mjs places inked cells into the committed npc_<id>.png and data/asset-manifest.json records their frames/populatedRows
seams.consumer: src/render/art.js sheetCell/drawSprite reads frames and populatedRows to choose the cell blitted
seams.roundTripProof: it loads the committed manifest and the committed NPC PNGs through the real createSheetLoader, calls the real drawSprite for each action row at index frames[r]-1 and past it, and asserts the blitted source cell is the last inked column of that row in the decoded committed PNG; the frame counts come from the manifest and the pixels, not from constants in the test.

entrypoints.realRunProof: it spawns `node tools/spritecut/build-characters.mjs <tmpdir>` from the repo with the real argv (ImageMagick on PATH, skipped only when magick is absent) and compares the PNGs it actually wrote to the committed sheets pixel for pixel.

rationale: The input fix, the column scan and the manifest update cannot land apart: with the right input but the hardcoded table, rows with a fourth cell keep ~68% of their ink and fail the 80% content bar; the scan without the right input re-commits blank rows; and the manifest must describe exactly the committed pixels or the rebuild-reproduces and sheetCell tests disagree. All three change the same committed NPC PNGs, so one ticket owns the single behaviour 'every authored NPC row and frame survives re-placement'. It depends on t-001 because its gate test runs measure-content.mjs, and on t-002 because it runs measure-edge/measure-jitter with each sheet's manifest frames. Render work is excluded because it is already on the branch and the captain kept it.
